destinations.name: Mellieha
destinations.tagline: Northern hilltop village above Malta's best-known sandy bay
destinations.summary: Mellieha looks down on the long sandy beach of Mellieha Bay, with Popeye Village, the Red Tower, Ghadira Nature Reserve and the Gozo ferry all close by.
destinations.html:
Mellieha (Il-Mellieha) sits on a ridge in the far north of Malta, overlooking Ghadira Bay. Visit Malta describes it as an isolated 15th-century hamlet that grew into a village, and it still has a village centre around its parish church, now ringed by hotels and holiday apartments. It is the main base for the north, the beaches of the Marfa peninsula and the crossing to Gozo and Comino.

The big draw is Mellieha Bay (Ghadira) below the village, a long sandy beach with shallow water that suits families. Behind it lies the Ghadira Nature Reserve, a wetland declared a bird sanctuary in 1978 and, as of November 2026, open to visitors between September and May. Beneath the parish church, the Chapel of the Blessed Virgin is a national shrine and a place of pilgrimage. Up on the Marfa ridge, the Red Tower (St Agatha's Tower) watches over both channels.

What to do

  • Spend a beach day at Mellieha Bay, or try quieter Paradise Bay, Armier Bay and Imgiebah Bay.
  • Visit Popeye Village, the film set on Anchor Bay, with children.
  • Walk the cliffs of the Majjistral Nature and History Park on the coastal paths.
  • Go birdwatching at Ghadira during the spring or autumn migration.

The ferry terminal at Cirkewwa, for Gozo and the boats to Comino, is a short drive north. Village feasts, including the celebrations around the Nativity of Our Lady in September, fill the square with bands and fireworks. St Paul's Bay is the next town south.

Mellieha is reached by road from the airport; allow extra time in traffic. Buses run from Valletta and the airport, but a hire car makes it much easier to reach the smaller bays. It suits families and travellers who want sand and countryside over city life.

destinations.name: Sliema
destinations.tagline: Seafront town of promenades, rock swimming and the Valletta ferry
destinations.summary: Sliema is Malta's main hotel and shopping town: a long seafront promenade, rocky swimming spots, Tigne Point and a ferry that crosses to Valletta in minutes.
destinations.html:
Sliema (Tas-Sliema) faces Valletta across Marsamxett Harbour on Malta's northeast coast. Once a fishing village and a summer retreat for Valletta families, it is now a dense town of apartment blocks, hotels, shops and cafes, and Visit Malta lists it among the island's main resorts. Its appeal is practical: a long seafront for walking, plenty of places to eat, and a direct public link to the capital.

Two waterfronts define the town. On the harbour side, The Strand looks straight across to the bastions of Valletta and Manoel Island; this is where the Valletta ferry and most harbour cruise boats depart. On the open-sea side, the Tower Road promenade runs northwest toward St Julian's, above flat limestone rocks where locals swim from ladders and small lidos in summer. Tigne Point, at the tip of the peninsula, has a shopping centre and the remains of an old fort.

What to do

  • Walk the promenade from Tigne Point to St Julian's in the late afternoon.
  • Take the harbour ferry to Valletta rather than the bus.
  • Join a Grand Harbour cruise or a Comino boat trip from The Strand.
  • Swim from the rocks on calm days, or try stand-up paddleboarding along the shore.

Sliema's coast is mostly rocky, but Exiles Bay includes a small sandy and pebble beach. For a larger sandy beach, take a bus to St George's Bay in St Julian's or head north to Golden Bay and Mellieha Bay. The rocky shore is pleasant on still days but can be dangerous when waves come in from the northeast, so watch the flags and local advice.

As a base, Sliema suits first-time visitors and anyone without a car. Hotels range from budget to upmarket, buses run along the seafront, and Valletta is a short boat ride away. Evenings are livelier than in the capital but calmer than Paceville next door. For a broader comparison of bases, see where to stay in Malta.

destinations.name: St Julian's
destinations.tagline: Bay town of Spinola's fishing boats and Paceville's nightlife
destinations.summary: St Julian's combines Spinola Bay's restaurants and fishing boats, the sandy St George's Bay and Paceville, the centre of Malta's nightlife, a walk from Sliema.
destinations.html:
St Julian's (San Giljan) runs along the northeast coast just beyond Sliema, and the two towns merge along a continuous seafront. It grew around a series of small bays: Balluta Bay with its apartment block and church, Spinola Bay with its moored fishing boats, and St George's Bay further north. Between them sits Paceville, a few streets of bars and clubs that form the centre of Malta's nightlife.

The town has three distinct moods. Spinola Bay is the place for dinner by the water, with colourful luzzu boats in the inlet and restaurants on all sides. Paceville comes alive late, especially at weekends and through the summer, and draws students, groups and language-school crowds. St George's Bay has a small sandy beach backed by hotels.

What to do

  • Swim at St George's Bay, then walk the seafront back toward Spinola.
  • Eat around Spinola Bay or Balluta Bay as the sun goes down.
  • Go out in Paceville, or skip it if you want a quiet night.
  • Book a scuba diving or sailing trip from the marina area.

Hotels here are mostly larger and more modern than in Valletta, from family resorts on St George's Bay to apartment rentals in the back streets. If you are a light sleeper, book away from Paceville. The UK government's travel advice notes pickpocketing on bus routes between Valletta and St Julian's, so keep bags closed on busy buses.

Buses link St Julian's with Valletta, the airport and the north. The Sliema ferry to Valletta is a walk or a short bus ride away. For beaches with more space, the sandy bays of the north, such as Golden Bay and Ghajn Tuffieha, are reachable by bus or a short drive, and St Paul's Bay is on the way.

destinations.name: St Paul's Bay
destinations.tagline: Northern resort of Bugibba, Qawra and the shipwreck islands
destinations.summary: St Paul's Bay, with Bugibba and Qawra, is Malta's main family resort area: seafront hotels, the National Aquarium, a perched beach and boat trips to Comino.
destinations.html:
St Paul's Bay (San Pawl il-Bahar) is a wide inlet on Malta's northeast coast and the name of the town that wraps around it. The resort districts of Bugibba and Qawra fill the eastern headland, and Visit Malta lists them among the island's main resorts. The bay takes its name from the tradition that the apostle Paul was shipwrecked nearby, on or near the small St Paul's Islands at its mouth, where a statue of the saint stands.

The area is built for holidays: hotels and apartments line a long promenade, with restaurants, supermarkets and tour desks in the streets behind. Swimming is mostly from rocks and lidos, plus the man-made Bugibba Perched Beach on the seafront. At Qawra Point, the Malta National Aquarium is an easy family outing, and the waters off the headland are popular for snorkelling and diving.

What to do

  • Visit the National Aquarium at Qawra Point, then walk the promenade.
  • Take a boat trip to Comino and the Blue Lagoon from the Bugibba waterfront.
  • Bus or drive to the sandy beaches of Golden Bay, Ghajn Tuffieha and Gnejna Bay on the west coast.
  • Look for waders at the Simar Nature Reserve in Xemxija, at the head of the bay.

Compare accommodation prices here with St Julian's and Valletta when planning a budget trip. The area stays fairly busy through the winter too. Evenings are relaxed, with bars and restaurants rather than clubs.

Bugibba has a bus terminus with direct routes to Valletta, the airport, Mdina and the Gozo ferry at Cirkewwa. The town is reached by road from the airport. Mellieha and its beaches are just to the northwest, and the Mosta Rotunda is a short ride inland.

destinations.name: The Three Cities
destinations.tagline: The Knights' first harbour towns: Birgu, Senglea and Cospicua
destinations.summary: The Three Cities of Birgu, Senglea and Cospicua face Valletta across the Grand Harbour: Fort St Angelo, the Inquisitor's Palace and quiet lanes reached by a short ferry.
destinations.html:
The Three Cities sit on the south side of the Grand Harbour, directly opposite Valletta. They are Vittoriosa, Senglea and Cospicua, known in Maltese as Il-Birgu, L-Isla and Bormla. The Order of St John made its first home here when it arrived in 1530, long before Valletta existed, and the harbour inlets between the towns have been in use since Phoenician times. Today the area is residential and much calmer than the capital, with narrow limestone lanes, small squares and a working waterfront.

Birgu holds most of the sights. Fort St Angelo stands at the end of the Birgu peninsula and dominated the defence of the harbour during the Great Siege of 1565. Inland, the Inquisitor's Palace is a museum of the Roman Inquisition in Malta. Across the creek, Senglea ends in the Gardjola Gardens, a small park with a stone lookout post facing Valletta.

What to do

  • Walk up through Fort St Angelo for its views back to the Valletta bastions.
  • Visit the Inquisitor's Palace, then wander the lanes of the Birgu collacchio behind it.
  • Stand at the Senglea point for the classic photograph of Upper Barrakka across the water.
  • Come in October for Birgufest, or on 8 September for the Victory Day Regatta in the harbour.

The easiest approach is by water. The Valletta harbour ferry runs between Valletta and Cospicua, and as of November 2026, its tickets include the lift up to the Upper Barrakka Gardens on the Valletta side. Traditional dghajsa water taxis also cross the harbour. Buses connect the Three Cities with the Valletta terminus if you prefer the road.

The prehistoric sites of the south are close by: the underground Hal Saflieni Hypogeum in Paola and the Tarxien Temples are a short drive inland. The fishing harbour of Marsaxlokk lies further southeast. Accommodation here is limited to a handful of guesthouses and small hotels, so most people visit as a half-day or day trip.

destinations.name: Valletta
destinations.tagline: Walled UNESCO capital of the Knights between two deep harbours
destinations.summary: Valletta is Malta's compact capital and a UNESCO World Heritage city: St John's Co-Cathedral, the Grandmaster's Palace and harbour views from the Upper Barrakka Gardens.
destinations.html:
Valletta sits on the Sceberras peninsula between Malta's two great natural harbours, the Grand Harbour to the east and Marsamxett Harbour to the west. The city is named after its founder, Grand Master Jean de Valette of the Order of St John, and building began in 1566, the year after the Great Siege. Its grid of steep, straight streets packs churches, palaces and auberges into an area small enough to explore on foot, which is why UNESCO lists the whole city as a World Heritage Site and calls it one of the most concentrated historic areas in the world.

The essential stop is St John's Co-Cathedral, the Knights' conventual church, plain outside and covered in gilded carving and inlaid marble tombstones within. A few streets away the Grandmaster's Palace was the seat of the Order's rulers, and the National Museum of Archaeology holds finds from Malta's prehistoric temples. At the tip of the peninsula, Fort St Elmo houses the National War Museum.

What to do

  • Start at the Upper Barrakka Gardens for the view across the Grand Harbour to the Three Cities.
  • Spend a slow hour inside St John's Co-Cathedral, then walk Republic Street and Merchants Street.
  • Take one of the Grand Harbour cruises to see the bastions from the water.
  • Try pastizzi or a ftira for lunch on the run.

The capital is also the transport hub. Many bus routes start or end at the terminus outside City Gate, harbour ferries cross to Sliema and to Cospicua in the Three Cities, and the fast ferry to Gozo leaves from the Grand Harbour. A lift links the Upper Barrakka Gardens with the waterfront below.

Valletta hosts many of the island's big dates, including Carnival, the fireworks festival over the Grand Harbour and Notte Bianca. It was European Capital of Culture in 2018. Hotels inside the walls are mostly small boutique conversions of old townhouses, so many visitors stay in Sliema and come across by ferry.

beaches.name: Armier Bay
beaches.tagline: Sandy Marfa beach facing Comino and Gozo
beaches.summary: A sandy bay on the Marfa peninsula with shallow water, beach kiosks and views to Comino. Pairs with Little Armier next door for a relaxed north-coast day.
beaches.html:
Armier Bay lies on the northern shore of the Marfa peninsula, the hilly tip of Malta beyond Mellieha. It is a sandy beach with shallow water that faces north toward Comino and Gozo, and its smaller neighbour, Little Armier, sits just to the east. Both are reached by road along the ridge, with a rural setting away from the main resort streets.

In summer the bay is organised, with sunbeds, umbrellas and a few beach kiosks and restaurants behind the sand, and it is a favourite with Maltese families who come for the whole day. The setting is rural: farmland, scrub and a scatter of summer boathouses rather than hotels. Because the beach faces north, it takes the brunt of the northerly wind when it blows, but on still days the water is clear and calm. Seagrass can wash ashore. The MTA explains that natural deposits are left on managed beaches in winter to support marine biodiversity.

Good to know

  • Best reached by car along the Marfa ridge road; parking behind the beach.
  • Bus service to the Marfa peninsula is limited: check Malta Public Transport before you go.
  • Sunbeds, umbrellas, kiosks and restaurants are listed locally; check availability before relying on them.
  • Little Armier is the neighbouring sandy bay.

Armier pairs well with the Red Tower on the ridge, with Paradise Bay near Cirkewwa and with Mellieha Bay below the town. Comino's Blue Lagoon is across the channel: see Comino boat trips and our Comino and Blue Lagoon guide.

beaches.name: Blue Lagoon
beaches.tagline: Comino's turquoise lagoon, by booked landing pass
beaches.summary: The shallow turquoise channel between Comino and Cominotto. Stepping ashore now needs a free timed landing pass booked online, and boat trips run from Malta and Gozo.
beaches.html:
The Blue Lagoon is the sheltered channel between Comino and the islet of Cominotto (Kemmunett), and it is the main reason most visitors come to Comino. The water is shallow and turquoise over white sand, and it has appeared on screen many times, including a diving scene in the film Swept Away and the mini-series Helen of Troy. The shore itself is mostly rock, with a small sandy patch, so on busy days space to sit is tight.

Booking a landing pass (as of November 2026)

Since May 2025, access to the lagoon is managed through an official online booking system, the Blue Lagoon Access Management System at blcomino.com, run under the tagline Book, Protect, Enjoy. As of November 2026 the official pages say:

  • Seasonal lifeguard provision is documented; check current duty notices before swimming. Cover is not guaranteed outside the season or duty hours.
  • Anyone who steps on land at the Blue Lagoon needs a landing pass (a QR code), including people arriving on private boats and tour boats.
  • The pass is free. You pick a date and one of three daily time slots: morning (08:00 to 13:00), afternoon (13:30 to 17:30) or sunset (18:00 to 22:00). The booking page shows slightly wider windows; the 30-minute difference is an allowance for boats arriving and leaving.
  • You can book up to two months ahead, for up to four people per reservation, and bookings cannot be changed. Same-day booking depends on availability.
  • Children under 5 with a parent or guardian do not need a pass.
  • Your QR code is scanned before you land; you get a wristband, which you return before you leave.
  • The ferry or boat is not included. Book it separately with a vessel authorised to serve the lagoon and make sure its times match your slot.

The Malta Tourism Authority caps the lagoon at 4,000 visitors at any one time and says entry without a valid booking may lead to a fine. A landing pass is not needed only to buy food or a drink and go straight back to your boat, or to pass through on the paved paths to other parts of Comino.

On the day

  • Public toilets and equipment hire are available; bring water and sun protection.
  • Shade is scarce on the rocks, and the sun reflects strongly off the water.
  • The morning and late slots are usually calmer than the middle of the day.

Most people arrive on Comino boat trips from Malta or Gozo; our Comino and Blue Lagoon guide covers departures and timing. Comino is car-free, so you can also walk from the lagoon to Santa Marija Bay or to the island's tower. The lagoon is also good for snorkelling and paddleboarding early in the day.

beaches.name: Bugibba Perched Beach
beaches.tagline: Man-made sand platform on the Bugibba seafront
beaches.summary: A man-made sandy beach raised above the rocks on the Bugibba promenade, with ladders into the sea. Central, easy to reach and handy for families.
beaches.html:
Bugibba Perched Beach is an artificial beach on the seafront promenade of Bugibba, close to where Bugibba meets Qawra. Instead of a natural bay, a sandy platform sits above the rocky shoreline, so you sunbathe on sand and reach the sea by ladders and steps from the rocks. VisitMalta lists it among the islands' Blue Flag beaches, and it gives the Bugibba and Qawra hotel strip a sandy option within walking distance.

The water off this stretch is deep and clear straight away, unlike the shallow sandy bays further north, so it suits confident swimmers more than toddlers paddling. The cafes, bars and restaurants of the promenade are right behind; check rental availability locally. Because it is in the middle of a resort, it is busy in summer so allow for crowds. When the sea is rough, the ladders can be difficult: follow the safety flags.

What to know

  • Sand platform above the rocks; sea entry by ladders and steps.
  • Deep water close in: best for confident swimmers.
  • Promenade cafes behind; check rental availability locally.
  • Buses 31, 45, 48 and TD13 link Valletta with Bugibba and St Paul's Bay.
  • Seasonal lifeguard coverage is listed by Malta Red Cross. As of November 2026, the season is closed; check local signs before swimming.

From the perched beach, follow the promenade to Qawra Point or to the Malta National Aquarium. Boat trips to Comino depart from the Bugibba jetty in season, and the sandy bays of Golden Bay and Mellieha Bay are a short bus ride away. See our where to stay in Malta guide if you are weighing up a base here.

beaches.name: Fomm ir-Rih Bay
beaches.tagline: Remote west-coast bay below Bahrija's cliffs
beaches.summary: A remote, undeveloped bay below the cliffs near Bahrija, with access that needs checking locally. Pebbly shore, clear water and a self-sufficient outing that needs local access checks.
beaches.html:
Fomm ir-Rih Bay (Fomm ir-Riħ) is a remote bay on Malta: a deep inlet on the west coast below the hamlet of Bahrija, on the Mgarr coast south of Gnejna Bay. High cliffs and clay slopes ring the bay, and the shore at the bottom is pebbles and rock rather than soft sand. Do not rely on services or lifeguard cover being available.

Getting down is part of the trip. Check the current public access route locally before setting out. Do not assume that a cliff-side path is open or safe; wear proper shoes and avoid wet conditions. The reward is clear, deep water for swimming and snorkelling and a sense of space that is hard to find elsewhere on the island. The bay faces northwest and is exposed to the sea: on rough days, do not swim. Bring water, food and shade, and carry your rubbish back up.

Know before you go

  • Check public access and path conditions locally before attempting the descent.
  • Pebble and rock shore: water shoes help.
  • Do not rely on facilities, shade or lifeguard cover.
  • Avoid when the wind is from the west and the sea is up.

Fomm ir-Rih is a natural stop on a west-coast walk (see coastal walking and hiking) and pairs with the cliff views at Dingli Cliffs further south. Base yourself in Mdina and Rabat, and for an easier swim nearby, head north to Gnejna Bay.

beaches.name: Ghajn Tuffieha Bay
beaches.tagline: Steps down to a reddish-gold bay below the clay slopes
beaches.summary: A sandy west-coast bay reached by a long flight of steps, framed by clay slopes and a watchtower. Quieter than Golden Bay next door, with fine sunsets.
beaches.html:
Ghajn Tuffieha Bay (Għajn Tuffieħa, also known as Riviera, the name of the bus stop above it) lies just south of Golden Bay on Malta's west coast. The sand is a warm reddish gold, the slopes behind it are bare clay and scrub, and an old coastal watchtower stands on the headland between the two bays. There is no road to the sand: you walk down a long flight of steps from the car park at the top, and that climb back up keeps the crowds lower than at its neighbour. VisitMalta lists it among the islands' Blue Flag beaches.

Malta Public Transport describes it as less crowded than Golden Bay, with a more tranquil feel and good sunset views, and that matches the experience on most days. A beach restaurant offers food, sunbeds and umbrellas, subject to availability. Like the rest of this coast, the bay is open to westerly wind, so the sea can be calm and clear one day and rough the next. The cliff paths and the Ghajn Tuffieha watchtower above are worth the detour before or after a swim.

Good to know

  • Access is by a long flight of steps from the car park; not suited to wheelchairs or heavy loads.
  • Bus 44 from Valletta and bus 223 from Bugibba run to the Golden Bay area, a short walk away.
  • Food service, sunbeds and umbrellas are subject to availability; bring water and sun protection.
  • Check the safety flags: the west coast picks up swell on windy days.
  • Seasonal lifeguard coverage is listed by Malta Red Cross. As of November 2026, the season is closed; check local signs before swimming.

Combine Ghajn Tuffieha with Golden Bay for facilities and with nearby Gnejna Bay. Check local path conditions before attempting a coastal walk. The trails of the Majjistral Nature and History Park begin a short way north, and Mellieha is the nearest resort town for an overnight stay.

beaches.name: Ghar Lapsi
beaches.tagline: South-coast cove affected by storm repairs, check access
beaches.summary: A small rocky cove and fishing hamlet on Malta's south coast, loved by swimmers and divers. Storm Harry damaged it in January 2026; confirm access before visiting.
beaches.html:
Ghar Lapsi (Għar Lapsi) is a small fishing hamlet on Malta's south coast, below the villages of Siggiewi and Qrendi and along the coast from the Blue Grotto. Għar means cave in Maltese. Before 2026 it was one of the island's favourite places for a swim off the rocks: a sheltered inlet of clear, calm water ringed by limestone, with steps and ladders into the sea and a shore entry that made it a standard training site for scuba divers.

Access update as of November 2026: check before travelling. Storm Harry damaged the bay in January 2026. Access was reported restricted in June 2026, and an October report described continuing works. An April 2026 report described a phased restoration project, covering the access ramp and steps, stabilising the cliff face where rock has fallen, rebuilding the slipway and jetties, and then paving and finishing work. A current official reopening or closure notice could not be verified. Do not plan a swim or dive here until the authorities confirm the bay has reopened.

What to know now

  • Storm Harry damaged the bay in January 2026; restoration works were reported continuing in October.
  • Current access and any reopening date could not be verified as of November 2026.
  • Follow all fencing and safety signs; the cliff and access paths were damaged.
  • Before the closure it was a rock-and-ladder swimming spot with no sand.

While access to Ghar Lapsi is uncertain, the south coast still has plenty to see: the cliff-top temples of Hagar Qim and Mnajdra and the boat trips into the Blue Grotto are close by. For a deep-water rock swim in the south, try St Peter's Pool near Marsaxlokk, and see snorkelling in Malta for other entry points.

beaches.name: Gnejna Bay
beaches.tagline: Rural west-coast bay with sand and flat rock ledges
beaches.summary: A sandy bay below Mgarr with flat rock shelves for sunbathing and boathouses by the shore. Quieter than Golden Bay, with a summer bus.
beaches.html:
Gnejna Bay (Il-Bajja tal-Ġnejna) sits at the end of a valley road below the village of Mgarr, on Malta's rural west coast. A strip of sand fills the head of the bay, and on either side flat, layered rock shelves run down to the water, which many locals prefer to the sand for sunbathing and for entering the sea. There are boathouses next to the shore. Malta Public Transport sums it up as a quieter beach destination with sandy shores and clear water.

The setting is farmland and clay slopes rather than hotels, and the bay is popular with Maltese families at weekends, when the road and car park fill. There is a kiosk by the shore. Confirm rental availability locally rather than relying on sunbed hire. The water is good for swimming and snorkelling along the rocky edges. The Il-Qarraba headland separates Gnejna from Ghajn Tuffieha Bay, and the Lippija watchtower stands on the ridge above the bay.

Getting there

  • By car: follow the road down from Mgarr to the car park by the beach.
  • By bus: route 101 serves Gnejna in summer only; from Valletta, take bus 44 to Mgarr and change.
  • Bring shade and water.
  • Rock shelves are uneven: water shoes help.
  • Seasonal lifeguard coverage is listed by Malta Red Cross. As of November 2026, the season is closed; check local signs before swimming.

Gnejna is a good half-day on its own or part of a west-coast loop with Golden Bay and Ghajn Tuffieha. The remote Fomm ir-Rih Bay lies further south toward Bahrija, and Mdina and Rabat are a short drive inland. For coast paths in the area, see coastal walking and hiking.

beaches.name: Golden Bay
beaches.tagline: Malta's west-coast sand beach with sunset views
beaches.summary: A wide sandy bay on Malta's west coast, below the Majjistral park cliffs. Easy road access, a direct bus from Valletta and sunsets over open sea.
beaches.html:
Golden Bay (Ir-Ramla tal-Mixquqa) is one of the sandy bays on Malta's northwest coast, near Manikata in the Mellieha area. A broad curve of golden sand faces west over open sea, so it catches the afternoon sun and the sunset, and the road runs almost to the sand. VisitMalta lists it among the islands' Blue Flag beaches.

The bay sits at the southern edge of the Majjistral Nature and History Park, Malta's first national park, and the clay slopes and garrigue above it are part of what makes the setting. The park's managers note that the dunes behind the beach are fragile and come under pressure on busy summer days, so keep to paths and off the vegetated sand. In summer the beach is organised, with sunbeds, umbrellas, watersports and food services, and a large hotel overlooks the northern end. Because the bay faces the open west coast, waves roll in on windy days: check the safety flags before you swim.

Before you go

  • Bus 44 runs from Valletta to Golden Bay; bus 223 links it with Bugibba.
  • Parking above the beach fills early on summer weekends.
  • Sunbeds, umbrellas, watersports and food services operate in season.
  • Follow the safety-flag colours: red means high hazard, double red means the water is closed.
  • Seasonal lifeguard coverage is listed by Malta Red Cross. As of November 2026, the season is closed; check local signs before swimming.

Golden Bay pairs with its quieter neighbour Ghajn Tuffieha Bay, a short walk south past the watchtower, and with Gnejna Bay beyond the headland. The cliff-top trails of the Majjistral park start nearby (see coastal walking and hiking), and the resort town of Mellieha with Mellieha Bay is a short drive north. For more options, see our best beaches in Malta guide.

beaches.name: Hondoq ir-Rummien
beaches.tagline: Clear-water cove below Qala, facing Comino
beaches.summary: A small cove below Qala in south-east Gozo with deep, clear water, ladders into the sea and views across to Comino. Popular with snorkellers, with sand, pebbles and rocky bathing areas.
beaches.html:
Hondoq ir-Rummien (Ħondoq ir-Rummien) is a small cove on the coast below the village of Qala, at the south-eastern corner of Gozo. It faces the channel towards Comino, so the view from the water takes in the smaller island and its tower. Visit Malta notes it is popular with snorkellers for its deep, clear water and the small caves at water level along the rocks.

There is a small patch of sand and pebbles, but most people swim off the rocks, where bathing ladders lead into the sea. The sand and pebble area offers shallower entry, while the rocky entry suits confident swimmers and snorkellers. The coastline nearby is dotted with traditional salt pans, some still worked in summer, which make a good short walk along the shore. Nature Trust Malta lists Hondoq as a Blue Flag beach, though the 2026 award could not be verified. It has public toilets and parking. Arrive early on summer weekends, when Gozitan families fill the limited space on the rocks.

What to expect

  • Seasonal lifeguard provision is documented; check current duty notices before swimming. Cover is not guaranteed outside the season or duty hours.
  • Small sand and pebble area and rocky shelves; check the current Blue Flag award locally.
  • Bathing ladders into deep, clear water; good snorkelling along the rocks.
  • Public toilets and parking above the cove.
  • Views across to Comino; salt pans along the nearby shore.

From Hondoq it is a short drive to Mgarr harbour, where the ferry to Malta leaves (see the Gozo ferry guide), and many Comino boat trips pass close by on the way to the Blue Lagoon. For a sandy beach on the same island, head north to Ramla Bay.

beaches.name: Imgiebah Bay (Selmun)
beaches.tagline: Sandy bay below Selmun for a self-sufficient visit
beaches.summary: A secluded sandy bay below the Selmun ridge, reached on foot down a rough track. Bring water, shade and good shoes; check access locally.
beaches.html:
Imgiebah Bay (Il-Bajja tal-Imġiebaħ) is a small, undeveloped bay on the north coast below Selmun, between Mellieha and St Paul's Bay. A patch of sand sits at the head of a green valley, with rocky shores on either side, and the bay looks out east across the open sea. Plan for a self-sufficient visit and check local access before setting out.

Approach from the Selmun area and check the current public walking route locally. Wear proper shoes and allow for an exposed return walk. The water is clear and good for swimming and snorkelling along the rocks when the sea is calm. Plan to bring everything you need, including plenty of water and shade, and take all your rubbish home. Seagrass can collect on the sand outside summer.

Before you set off

  • Check the public walking route locally and wear proper shoes.
  • Do not rely on facilities, lifeguard cover or shade being available.
  • Carry water, sun cover and a bag for your litter.
  • Avoid the walk in the midday heat in July and August.

Imgiebah makes a good half-day from Mellieha or St Paul's Bay. If you want facilities afterwards, Mellieha Bay is a short drive west. For more walks like this one, see coastal walking and hiking, and for a quieter west-coast option try Fomm ir-Rih Bay.

beaches.name: Mellieha Bay (Ghadira)
beaches.tagline: Long shallow sandy beach at Malta's northern end
beaches.summary: A long sandy beach with shallow, gently shelving water below Mellieha, opposite the Ghadira Nature Reserve. Malta's go-to family beach in summer.
beaches.html:
Mellieha Bay, known locally as Ghadira (Għadira), is the long sandy beach at the head of the bay below the town of Mellieha, in the north of Malta. The water shelves very gently and stays shallow a long way out, which is why it is the beach many Maltese families choose for small children. VisitMalta lists Ghadira Bay among the islands' Blue Flag beaches.

In summer the sand is fully organised: sunbeds and umbrellas, watersports operators, beach bars and kiosks run along its length, and it gets busy on weekends and in August. The main road runs right behind the beach, with bus stops and roadside parking. Across that road is the Ghadira Nature Reserve, a protected wetland run by BirdLife Malta and a good contrast to the beach. Conditions vary with wind and swell, so check the beach safety flags before entering the water.

Planning your visit

  • Shallow, gently shelving water suits families with young children.
  • Sunbeds, umbrellas, watersports and kiosks in season.
  • Bus route 101 stops at Ghadira; routes to Cirkewwa pass along the bay.
  • Arrive early on summer weekends for parking and space.
  • Seasonal lifeguard coverage is listed by Malta Red Cross. As of November 2026, the season is closed; check local signs before swimming.

From Mellieha Bay it is a short hop to Popeye Village in Anchor Bay and up the Marfa ridge to the Red Tower. For quieter sand, try Armier Bay or Paradise Bay further north, or walk down to Imgiebah Bay below Selmun. Ferries to Gozo leave from nearby Cirkewwa (see the Gozo ferry guide).

beaches.name: Mgarr ix-Xini
beaches.tagline: Quiet fjord-like inlet with a pebble beach
beaches.summary: A narrow inlet at the end of a deep gorge on Gozo's south coast, with a small shingle beach, calm clear water and a 17th-century watchtower at its mouth.
beaches.html:
Mgarr ix-Xini (Mġarr ix-Xini) is a long, narrow inlet on the south coast of Gozo, between Xewkija, Sannat and Ghajnsielem. A prehistoric river cut the deep gorge that leads down to it, and the inlet is so sheltered that the Knights of St John used it as a galley harbour. A small watchtower, built in 1661, still guards the mouth of the bay. More recently, the inlet was a location for the 2015 film By the Sea, shot here in 2014.

The beach itself is a small strip of shingle at the head of the inlet, and much of the swimming is off the rocks along the sides. The water is usually calm, and it is a known site for snorkelling and diving: Visit Malta notes rare fish on the western side of the inlet entrance, and caverns at around 10 and 16 metres that divers can reach from here. It is also a good, sheltered place to launch a kayak and paddle out to the tower. Mgarr ix-Xini stays one of Gozo's quieter bathing spots, though local families and visiting boats fill it on summer weekends.

What to know

  • Seasonal lifeguard provision is documented; check current duty notices before swimming. Cover is not guaranteed outside the season or duty hours.
  • Small shingle beach with rock ledges along the sides; footwear helps.
  • Calm, clear water suited to snorkelling, diving and kayaking.
  • Reached by a narrow, winding road down the valley; parking is limited.
  • Facilities are limited; check what is open outside summer.

Combine Mgarr ix-Xini with sea kayaking along the south coast or a walk on the cliffs; see coastal walking and hiking. It is close to Mgarr harbour for the ferry back to Malta, and the livelier resort inlet of Xlendi Bay lies further west.

beaches.name: Paradise Bay
beaches.tagline: Small sandy cove reached by steps near Cirkewwa
beaches.summary: A small sandy cove below the cliffs near the Cirkewwa ferry terminal, reached by steps. A compact beach with a lido beside the sand.
beaches.html:
Paradise Bay is a small, sheltered cove on Malta's northwest tip, a few minutes from the Cirkewwa ferry terminal. A short crescent of sand sits at the foot of the cliffs, and the water is clear, with rocky edges that suit snorkelling. The government bathing-water profile distinguishes this cove from the beach opposite Paradise Bay Resort Hotel.

You reach the sand down a flight of steps from the parking area at the top, so pack light. The cove is small, and in summer a beach concession with sunbeds, umbrellas and a snack bar offers rentals beside the sand. Space can be limited on hot days. Outside peak season it is far quieter. The rocky coast around Cirkewwa is also a popular dive area, which is why you will often see divers kitting up nearby (see scuba diving).

What to expect

  • Steps down from the parking area; not step-free.
  • Small sandy cove with clear water and rocky edges for snorkelling.
  • Seasonal sunbeds, umbrellas and snack bar; the cove fills early in summer.
  • Buses to Cirkewwa (route 42 from Valletta, route 101 along the north) stop a short walk away.

Paradise Bay is handy before or after the ferry: see the Gozo ferry guide, or book one of the Comino boat trips from the north coast. Nearby, the Marfa ridge has Armier Bay and the Red Tower, and Mellieha Bay is a short drive back toward Mellieha.

beaches.name: Pretty Bay
beaches.tagline: Birzebbuga's town-centre sandy beach
beaches.summary: Birzebbuga's sandy town beach in south-east Malta, with shops, cafes and restaurants along the seafront. Easy access and one of the larger sandy beaches on Malta.
beaches.html:
Pretty Bay is the town beach of Birzebbuga (Birżebbuġa), a small seaside resort in south-east Malta a short drive from Marsaxlokk. It has been a favourite bathing spot for Maltese families for decades, though it looks different today from how it once did. According to the Malta Tourism Authority, there was almost no sand here until some years ago and bathers swam off flat rocks and platforms; the bay was later filled with sand recovered from the seabed during dredging for a nearby project. The result is one of the larger sandy beaches on Malta.

Because the beach sits right in the town centre, it is convenient to reach and to spend a day at. Cafes, bars, restaurants and shops line the promenade behind the sand, and the bay is listed by Visit Malta as a venue for watersports such as windsurfing. It is a local's beach rather than a resort strip, busiest on summer weekends and evenings when families come down after work. The water shelves gently from the sand, which suits children and paddlers. Across the water you will see the cranes of the Malta Freeport, so this is a practical, convenient beach rather than a scenic one.

Good to know

  • Seasonal lifeguard provision is documented; check current duty notices before swimming. Cover is not guaranteed outside the season or duty hours.
  • Sandy beach in the centre of Birzebbuga with a promenade behind it.
  • Bars, cafes, restaurants, shops and public toilets close by; parking in town.
  • Visit Malta lists the bay as a venue for watersports including windsurfing; check local availability.
  • Calm, shallow water near the shore is good for families.

Pretty Bay pairs well with the rock swimming at St Peter's Pool on the Delimara peninsula and a fish lunch in Marsaxlokk. The south's big prehistoric sites, Hagar Qim and Mnajdra, and the sea caves of the Blue Grotto are a short drive west along the coast.

beaches.name: Ramla Bay
beaches.tagline: Gozo's largest sandy bay, with red-gold sand
beaches.summary: Gozo's largest sandy bay: deep red-gold sand below terraced hills, clear water and no hotels behind it. Seasonal lifeguards and snack bars are documented here.
beaches.html:
Ramla Bay (Ir-Ramla l-Ħamra, the red sandy beach) sits on the north coast of Gozo, between the villages of Xaghra and Nadur. Visit Malta calls it Gozo's largest sandy bay, and the colour is what most people remember: a deep, reddish-gold sand backed by countryside and steep terraced hillsides, with no hotels or tourist developments behind the beach. Calypso's Cave sits on the hillside above.

Swimming is generally easy here. The water is clear, and there are some smooth underwater boulders a few metres out in the central strip that are simple to swim around. On windy days, surf rolls in from the north, which children enjoy but which also means you should watch the beach flags and stay within your depth. Look out for the white statue of the Virgin Mary on the sand, the remains of a Roman building buried near the cafes, and an 18th-century fougasse, a rock-cut mortar the Knights built to defend the bay. Visit Malta lists lifeguard services here. Check the beach notices for current seasonal cover.

What to know before you go

  • Seasonal lifeguard provision is documented; check current duty notices before swimming. Cover is not guaranteed outside the season or duty hours.
  • Listed by Nature Trust Malta as a Blue Flag beach; the 2026 award could not be verified.
  • Lifeguards in the summer season, plus snack bars, toilets, equipment hire and parking.
  • The easiest approach is by road from Nadur or Xaghra through the valley.
  • Natural setting with little built shade: bring or hire an umbrella.

Ramla is a natural stop on a Gozo day that takes in the Ggantija Temples in Xaghra and the Cittadella in Victoria. For a smaller, wilder red-sand cove, San Blas Bay is just along the coast to the east. Plan the crossing with our Gozo ferry guide and the wider Gozo travel guide.

beaches.name: San Blas Bay
beaches.tagline: Small red-sand cove at the foot of a steep Nadur valley
beaches.summary: A small cove of reddish sand below Nadur on Gozo's north-east coast, reached on foot down a steep lane. Quiet, good for snorkelling, with few facilities.
beaches.html:
San Blas Bay is a small cove on the north-east coast of Gozo, in the territory of Nadur, a little east of Ramla Bay. The sand has the same reddish tint as Ramla's, but the setting is tighter and wilder: a narrow beach at the foot of a green, terraced valley, with rocks at either end. Visit Malta lists the coves of the Nadur coast among Gozo's good spots for snorkelling and the San Blas valley among the island's best walking areas.

The way down is the reason the beach stays quieter. You leave the car at the top and walk down a narrow, very steep lane to the sand, and the climb back up in summer heat is hard work, so it is not a good choice for anyone with limited mobility or with lots of gear to carry. The reward is a less crowded beach with clear water. Snorkellers should head for the rocks at the sides of the cove. Visit Gozo lists deckchair hire and a small refreshment kiosk; check availability and bring water, food and shade, and take everything away when you leave.

Planning a visit

  • Reddish sand with rocks at both ends of the cove.
  • Steep walk down from parking at the top; the return climb is tough.
  • Deckchair hire and a small kiosk are listed by Visit Gozo; check seasonal availability.
  • Best for a quieter swim and for snorkelling around the rocks.

San Blas works well as part of a walking day on Gozo's north-east coast; see coastal walking and hiking for routes. If you want the same sand with lifeguards and cafes, Ramla Bay is close by, and the rock swimming at Hondoq ir-Rummien looks across to Comino from the south-east corner of the island.

beaches.name: Santa Marija Bay
beaches.tagline: Comino's quieter sandy bay on the north coast
beaches.summary: A small sandy bay on Comino's north coast, a walk across the car-free island from the Blue Lagoon. Clear water and a calmer alternative to the lagoon's crowds.
beaches.html:
Santa Marija Bay (St Mary's Bay) is a small sandy bay on the north-east coast of Comino, the 3.5-square-kilometre island between Malta and Gozo. Visit Malta lists it as one of the most popular bathing spots on Comino, alongside San Niklaw Bay and the famous Blue Lagoon. It has a short strip of sand and clear water that shelves into the bay.

Because Comino has no cars and only a handful of buildings, getting here is part of the trip. Most people combine it with a boat trip to the Blue Lagoon and walk across the island on its dirt tracks, which takes you through garigue scented with wild thyme. The bay is noticeably calmer than the lagoon on a summer afternoon. Check which facilities are available and bring water, food and shade, and carry your rubbish back with you. Outside summer, Comino is quiet and good for walkers and photographers.

Visiting Santa Marija Bay

  • Seasonal lifeguard provision is documented; check current duty notices before swimming. Cover is not guaranteed outside the season or duty hours.
  • Small sandy beach with clear water on Comino's north-east coast.
  • Arrive by boat or walk across the island on tracks.
  • Check current facilities and bring water, food and shade.
  • Check how your landing at the Blue Lagoon works before you set off (see below).

If you land at the Blue Lagoon, you need a landing pass only to stay at the lagoon itself; walking straight through on the paved paths to other parts of Comino does not require one, according to the official booking site. Our Comino and Blue Lagoon guide explains the boats, and coastal walking and hiking covers routes across the island.

beaches.name: St George's Bay
beaches.tagline: St Julian's town beach, Malta's first Blue Flag
beaches.summary: A small sandy town beach in St Julian's, steps from Paceville's hotels and bars. Malta's first Blue Flag beach, with frequent buses from Valletta.
beaches.html:
St George's Bay is the sandy town beach of St Julian's, at the foot of Paceville. It is compact, a short arc of sand inside a sheltered inlet ringed by hotels, restaurants and the nightlife streets behind, making it a convenient beach if you are staying in St Julian's or Sliema. According to the Malta Tourism Authority, it earned Malta's first Blue Flag in 2009 and has kept the award every year since.

Check swimming conditions and local safety flags before entering the water. In summer the sand is busy from morning, with cafes and restaurants close by, and the crowd gets younger and louder as the day goes on. It is a practical swim between sightseeing days rather than a scenic escape. Watch the safety flags: the lifesaving boundary is marked with red-over-yellow flags, and a double red flag means the water is closed.

Visiting St George's Bay

  • Blue Flag beach in the centre of the St Julian's hotel district.
  • Cafes, shops and restaurants behind the sand; check any rental services locally.
  • Buses 13, 13A, 14, 16, 21 and TD13 run from Valletta to Sliema and St Julian's.
  • Arrive early in July and August, when the small beach fills quickly.
  • Seasonal lifeguard coverage is listed by Malta Red Cross. As of November 2026, the season is closed; check local signs before swimming.

From St George's Bay, walk along the seafront to Spinola Bay and on to Sliema, or take a boat across to Valletta. Day trips to Comino and Grand Harbour cruises leave from the Sliema waterfront nearby. For sandier, wilder bays, head north to Golden Bay or Mellieha Bay.

beaches.name: St Peter's Pool
beaches.tagline: Natural rock pool on the Delimara peninsula
beaches.summary: A deep natural swimming pool cut into flat limestone on the Delimara peninsula near Marsaxlokk. Clear water, sun-warmed rock shelves, no sand; do not rely on lifeguard cover.
beaches.html:
St Peter's Pool (often signed simply as Peter's Pool) is a natural rock pool on the Delimara peninsula, the headland that closes off the eastern side of the bay at Marsaxlokk. The Malta Tourism Authority describes Delimara as having two secluded rocky inlets suitable for swimming, and this is the better known of the two. There is no beach here in the usual sense: you lie out on wide, flat shelves of pale limestone and drop straight into deep, very clear water.

That deep water is the appeal and the main thing to plan around. The pool is a natural rock inlet with no sand and an uneven entry; do not rely on lifeguard cover, so it suits confident swimmers. Younger children need close supervision at the edge, and you should judge the sea for yourself: on days with a strong south-easterly swell the inlet becomes rough and getting out over the rock is harder. Some visitors jump from the rocks; check the depth below before you do, and never jump where you cannot see the bottom clearly. Official travel advice warns of rockfalls here, so keep to the open rock shelf and respect any fencing or warning signs.

Before you go

  • A natural rock pool: no sand and deep water from the edge; do not rely on lifeguard cover.
  • Bring water, sun cover and something soft to lie on; there is little or no shade on the rock.
  • Reached by narrow country roads across the Delimara peninsula, with a walk down to the water at the end.
  • Calmest on still mornings; avoid it in a rough south-easterly sea.

Pair a swim with lunch in Marsaxlokk, whose fishing harbour and Sunday fish market are a short drive back along the peninsula; local fish dishes such as aljotta and lampuki pie are what to look for. The sandy alternative nearby is Pretty Bay in Birzebbuga, and the coastal walks of Xrobb l-Ghagin Nature Park lie on the far side of the peninsula. For more swimming options across the islands, see our guide to the best beaches in Malta.

beaches.name: Xlendi Bay
beaches.tagline: Cliff-framed inlet and resort on Gozo's west coast
beaches.summary: A narrow inlet at the end of a deep valley on Gozo's west coast, with deep, clear water off the rocks, cafes on the waterfront and sunset views from the cliffs.
beaches.html:
Xlendi Bay is a sea inlet on the south-west coast of Gozo, at the end of a deep, green valley that was once a river bed. Until the mid-20th century it was a small fishing port; today it is one of Gozo's main resorts, but a compact one, with steep cliffs on both sides of the bay and restaurants, cafes and apartments around the waterfront. On the promontory stands Xlendi Tower, built in 1650, above a coast of hand-cut salt pans.

There is a small patch of sand at the head of the bay, but most swimming here is off the rocks, using ladders into deep, very clear water. On the left side of the bay, two levels of rock pathway give you room to walk and to lay out a towel. Xlendi is a well-known spot for diving and snorkelling: a reef in the middle of the bay rises to within a metre of the surface. Climb the steps up the cliff to the right of the bay for the best views, especially at sunset.

Good to know

  • Seasonal lifeguard provision is documented; check current duty notices before swimming. Cover is not guaranteed outside the season or duty hours.
  • Mostly rock swimming with ladders; a small sandy area at the head of the bay.
  • Restaurants, cafes, toilets, parking and equipment hire on the waterfront.
  • Dive schools and snorkelling sites, including Xlendi Cave, in the bay.
  • Stairs up the cliffs give views over the bay and Xlendi Tower.

Xlendi is a short drive from Victoria and the Cittadella, and the coastline of Dwejra and the Inland Sea lies further north-west. For a quieter inlet on the same coast, try Mgarr ix-Xini to the east. Our Gozo travel guide covers where to stay on the island.
